title: Latency-credit hybrid batcher - sketch
content:
Purpose and motivation:

This is a working sketch for a hybrid continuous batching scheduler that trades off between per-request latency budgets and aggregate throughput with an explicit crediting model for fairness. The goal is to provide an operationally simple controller that:
- respects soft per-request latency targets when possible,
- maintains high GPU efficiency via larger token batches when workload permits, and
- enforces fairness across customers/tenants and request classes with a predictable notion of backlog debt.

Why another variant?
Existing sketches in the folder explore token-level vs request-level batching and token apportioners. This draft focuses on a credit-based hybrid that: (1) treats requests as first-class objects with latency budgets, (2) accrues token-serving credits over time to allow low-priority/cheap requests to accumulate capacity for larger efficient batches, and (3) incorporates KV-cache warmness and kernel affinity into admission/packing heuristics. The hope: better end-to-end SLO adherence for interactive flows while sustaining throughput for high-volume background workloads.

Constraints and assumptions:
- GPU kernels are more efficient with larger homogeneous token batches (same model variant, quantization profile, and sequence length distribution).
- KV cache hits reduce per-token cost and can shift the batch size sweet spot.
- Workload contains mixture of interactive (strict latency), background (high throughput), and streaming chat sessions (continuous open requests).
- Scheduler runs at ~1–10ms cadence for fast paths, with coarser decisions for heavyweight packing.

Core ideas overview:
1) Latency budget per request: each incoming request r is assigned a soft latency budget B_r (ms). Budgets are derived from API tier (interactive vs background), route config, and configured SLOs. Budget is split into: queuing allowance (Q_r) and execution allowance (E_r).
2) Credit accrual: each logical tenant / route has a credit balance C_t that accrues at a configured rate (credits per ms) when the tenant is not consuming tokens. Credits are denominated in "servable token units" (roughly proportional to tokens * kernel-cost-factor).
3) Hybrid admission: a request can be scheduled immediately if either:
   a) its remaining queuing allowance Q_r is near zero (priority to meet latency budget), or
   b) the tenant's credit balance C_t exceeds a dynamic per-batch minimum and kernel-affinity constraints allow cheap packing.
4) Kernel affinity and KV-aware packing: when forming a batch, prefer items that share kernel characteristics and similar KV-cache warmness (e.g., cached prefix vs cold). For mixed warmness, estimate effective per-token cost and prefer grouping with similar cost factors.
5) Fairness / debt: tenants can go into debt (negative C_t) up to a configurable limit. Debt accrues a penalty that reduces future accrual rates (soft throttling) until balance is restored.

Detailed components:

A. Budget derivation and sliding queuing window
- On arrival, assign B_r = base_slo(route) * tier_multiplier. Example: interactive route base 120ms, tier x1.0 => 120ms.
- Reserve a small fixed execution budget E_r = expected_model_latency(model, seq_len) * 1.15 + buffer_ms. Q_r = B_r - E_r.
- The scheduler maintains a short sliding window W (default 5ms) where it will hold requests for packing if Q_r > W and C_t < min_batch_credit. Requests with Q_r <= W are flagged as pending-expedite.

B. Credit model
- Credit accrual: dC_t/dt = alpha_t (credits/ms). alpha_t is configured by plan/route; e.g., background-heavy tenants get high alpha.
- Credit unit: 1 credit ~= cost of serving 1 1-token step on baseline kernel. For heterogeneous kernels, we use kernel_cost_factor kcf in credit arithmetic.
- When scheduling a batch of N tokens for tenant t with kernel k, we deduct N * kcf from C_t.
- Debt: C_t may go negative down to -D_max. When C_t < 0, accrual rate scales by exp(-beta * |C_t|) to gradually slow further debt.

C. Packing heuristic (batch formation)
- Candidate pool: requests within the current holding window. For each candidate compute: remaining tokens to produce, estimated kernel (k), kv_warmness score w in [0,1], priority p derived from Q_r, and tenant credit C_t.
- Score function S = w * (1 + log(1 + C_t)) * affinity_factor(k) - lambda * expedite_flag.
- Greedy pack: sort candidates by S descending and add until token cap or kernel homogeneity threshold crossed. If expedite_flag set (low Q_r), forcibly add top expedite requests even if scoring low.
- Post-pack fairness check: ensure no tenant exceeds per-batch token cap; if so, trim low-priority entries and leave them for the next window.

D. KV cache interplay
- For requests with warm prefixes (w >= 0.8) we assume effective per-token kernel cost is reduced by factor g(w). This makes grouping warm items beneficial because they help expand batch size without proportionally increasing execution time.
- Metric to expose: effective_tokens = raw_tokens * g(w). Credits consumed = effective_tokens * kcf.

E. Kernel selection and multi-kernel batches
- Prefer single-kernel batches for efficiency. When beneficial, allow multi-kernel pack if the incremental overhead (kernel-switch cost) is offset by higher GPU utilization. Maintain threshold T_kernel_switch (ms).

Simplified scheduler loop (pseudocode as text):
- every tick (t_interval ~ 2ms):
  - ingest new requests into waiting_pool
  - update C_t for all tenants (accrue)
  - mark expedite requests (Q_r <= W)
  - build candidate list (waiting_pool where Q_r > 0)
  - while GPU capacity available and candidate list non-empty:
      - pick seed candidate with highest S
      - try greedy pack around seed (respect kernel affinity and per-batch token cap)
      - if expedite present and not included, inject up to expedite_limit slots
      - submit batch, deduct credits, update metrics

Metrics to track (per-tenant and global):
- p50/p95/p99 queuing latency, execution latency, end-to-end latency
- credit balance distribution over time (histogram)
- effective token throughput and GPU utilization per kernel
- kernel-switch overhead rate and time spent in mixed-kernel batches
- KV warmness hit-rate and effective g(w) observed

Safety and SLO fallback behaviors:
- If the cluster is saturated and expedite queues grow, enable immediate-exec mode for interactive tiers: ignore credit checks and schedule as quickly as possible. Track cost/cpu and raise alerts.
- Implement per-tenant hard limits to avoid single tenant monopolization even with positive credits.

Experiment plan / evaluation:
- Offline trace-driven simulator: run scheduler variants (credited-hybrid vs token-only vs request-only) on 7-day production traces with labeled route tiers. Measure end-to-end latency SLO misses and token-throughput.
- Microbench: synthetic mix to validate kernel affinity heuristics and kernel-switch cost model; vary KV hit rates to quantify g(w).
- Canary: deploy as opt-in route under serving-runtime canary pool for targeted customers. Monitor cost regressions and SLOs for 24–72 hrs.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Credit granularity: credits expressed in token-steps may not map linearly across diverse kernels (quantized kernels, FlashAttention variants). How to normalize cross-kernel cost robustly?
- Debt semantics: should debt be allowed to exceed D_max if tenant is premium (enterprise)? If so, use per-tenant policy.
- Streaming sessions: long-lived chat sessions continuously accrue Q_r semantics. How to prevent starvation of background work when many live streams slowly consume tokens? Need explicit background quotas or token-shed policies.
- Interaction with autoscaler: large credit accumulations can create sudden bursty demand; autoscaler must consider credit backlog as a signal.

Next steps:
- Implement simulator harness and target metrics (owner: Maya).
- Prototype scheduler loop in a branch, keep kernel packing simple first, add KV warmness later (owner: Jordan).
- Run trace experiments and iterate on S and g(w) parameters (owner: Evan).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally exploratory: looking for feedback on the credit math, debt/backpressure behavior, and operational signals we should surface in the Console (tokens-to-credit visualization, tenant debt alerts).
- Related items: see linked Jira for kernel cost calibration tasks and PR for small-packer helper functions.

End of sketch.
